slice: A7 process wiring slice 3: automatic revalidation after approval and WF07 PR preparation
author: Claude Code (Opus 5.5)
decision: user 2026-11-21: revalidation starts automatically after approval; WF07 runs automatic preparation (no GitHub write)
flow: relay every 5s: advance_once (skipped while stopping) then sync_once; one delivery per tick

advance_once, at most one step: approved -> ledger.revalidate as the approver (plan requester); proposal_ready without a WF07 record -> ImageRecoveryPRBridge.prepare (local exact diff/PR payload, no publish)
no repetition: interrupted revalidation times out to needs_review; a WF07 record is never prepared twice
revalidation_seconds <= 15 (RELAY_BLOCK_SECONDS) validated in config so one tick stays inside the 30s relay progress age
RecoveryOutbox.enqueue_pr: fixed texts for prepared/no_pr/needs_review/cancelled; no URL, head or diff; reason only if [a-z_]
retention includes the WF07 record prune when a bridge is attached
entrypoint passes no pr_bridge (no live GitHub/CI/ECR readers or Slack->GitHub mapping yet) and the observe port stays unconnected

mutation_checks.false_kill_note: first run with two extra modules reported 'page state filter ignored' as killed due to a transient failure elsewhere; it actually survived; a dedicated state-filter test was added and now kills it

full_suite.earlier_run: 1741 passed before the WF07 retention addition (log a7-advance-full.log)

known_behaviour: after preparation, the ledger's observation freshness expires and a needs_review (observation_expired) notice follows; real state, wording to be revisited with the publication path
a requester without a GitHub mapping is refused without a WF07 record; the refusal can repeat every 5s until fresh_until (no reads)
a WF07 record interrupted in 'preparing' stays until the existing interrupt path (not wired)
approver must be the plan requester (existing WF06 restriction)
no_external_actions: no cluster, GitHub write besides this PR, deploy, Slack, incident drill, Terraform, paid model call
